documents.title: Antora Environment :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Antora Environment Antora is our static website generator. We use it to generate the documentation of the project It is part of the documentation of Feel++ docs website. To generate the documentation $ npm install (1) $ npm run antora (2) $ npm run start (3) 1 Install the dependencies 2 Generate the documentation 3 Serve the documentation, the URL is provided in the console

documents.title: CMake Environment :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf CMake Environment The CMakeLists.txt is setup with Feel++. A sample Feel++ application is available in src. 1. Building The CMakeLists.txt is configured to build the application in src. The following commands can be used to build the application: $ cmake --preset default (1) $ cmake --build --preset default (2) $ cmake --build --preset default -t install (3) 1 Configure the project 2 Build the project 3 Install the project 2. Packaging CPack is configured and allows to generate a binary and source package. Use the following commands to generate the binary package: $ cmake --build --preset default -t package Use the following commands to generate the source package: $ cmake --build --preset default -t package_source 3. Testing CTest is configured. Use the following command to run the tests: $ cmake --build --preset default -t test

documents.title: GitHub Actions :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf GitHub Actions GitHub Actions are set up to build the documentation using Antora and upload them to docs.feelpp.org[Feel++ docs] upon any change in the repo. build, install, package and deliver the Feel++ code See the [workflow file](.github/workflows/ci.yml) for more details. 1. Skipping a job You can skip the CI by adding the following line in the commit message: [skip ci] You can skip the job that build the documentation by adding the following line in the commit message: doc skip. You can skip the job that build the code by adding the following line in the commit message: code skip.

documents.title: VS Code Integration :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf VS Code Integration The project is configured to integrate VSCode using Docker Container. The Docker image can be set from feelpp/feelpp or feelpp/feelpp-toolboxes, simply edit .devcontainer/Dockerfile and choose the image you want. ssh-keyscan is used on github.com to register the public key of github in $HOME/.ssh/known_hosts and avoid having git auth issues the first time we log into the container and push/pull to/from github. The following extensions are installed in Docker: cpptools cmaketools cmake asciidoctor-vscode

documents.title: Problem Set 1: RB for Linear Affine Elliptic Problems :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Problem Set 1: RB for Linear Affine Elliptic Problems We consider the problem of designing a thermal fin to effectively remove heat from a surface. The two-dimensional fin, shown in Figure 1, consists of a vertical central “post” and four horizontal “subfins”; the fin conducts heat from a prescribed uniform flux “source” at the root, \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{root}}\) , through the large-surface-area subfins to surrounding flowing air. The fin is characterized by a five-component parameter vector, or “input,” \(\mu_ = (\mu_1 , \mu_2, \ldots, \mu_5 )\),where \(\mu_i = k^i , i = 1, \ldots , 4\), and \(\mu_5 = \mathrm{Bi}\); \(\mu\) may take on any value in a specified design set \(D \subset \mathbb{R}^5\). Figure 1. Thermal fin Here \(k^i\) is the thermal conductivity of the ith subfin (normalized relative to the post conductivity \(k^0 \equiv 1\)); and \(\mathrm{Bi}\) is the Biot number, a nondimensional heat transfer coefficient reflecting convective transport t

documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Problem Set 3: A Posteriori Error Bounds, Greedy Sampling Procedure We consider again the problem of designing a thermal fin of Problem Set 1 and 2. Given the reduced basis approximation implemented in PS2, we turn to implementing the associated a posteriori error estimation procedures developed in the lecture. The second half of this problem set is devoted to implementing the greedy sampling procedure. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf M2 ROM & Data-Driven ROM How can a numerical model predict fast enough, assess its accuracy, and learn from measurements? This course develops methods useful for digital twins through lectures and hands-on notebook work. Master CSMI · Université de Strasbourg · Christophe Prud’homme 1. Start here Session 1 — Digital twins: models, observations and prediction Thursday 10 September 2026, 13:30–15:30 (Europe/Paris). Prepare your notebook environment and download the opening notebook. Read the notation guide and the mathematical reminders whenever you need the distinction between a function and its coefficients, the fixed norm and the parameter-energy norm, or a state and a functional. Both are always available in Notation and reminders at the top of the navigation. 2. Introduction The Kalman filter is a powerful mathematical tool used for estimating the state of a dynamic system from a series of noisy measurements. It is widely applied in areas like control systems, robotics, navigation, and finance. This session will guide you through implementing the Kalman filter with two simple examples: One-Dimensional Position Tracking Two-Dimensional Position and Velocity Estimation By the end of this session, you’ll understand how the Kalman filter works and how to implement it in practice. 2. PBDW combines a low-dimensional background space with an update determined by measurements. The background is a space of plausible states; its coefficients are inferred from data, not supplied by the unknown true state. Riesz representatives and stability Each sensor is a bounded linear functional represented in the state inner product by a vector. documents.title: Digital twins: connecting models and observations :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Digital twins: connecting models and observations A useful numerical model answers a question about a physical system. A digital-twin setting adds observations of that system and a process for updating the digital representation as the system evolves. Begin with a purpose Consider a heated component monitored by a few temperature sensors. We want to estimate its temperature field, predict a quantity such as a peak temperature, and decide whether a proposed operating condition is acceptable. The sensors observe only part of the state; the model supplies information between sensors and supports predictions under changed conditions. For this material, a digital twin is a digital representation associated with a physical system, informed by observations and used for a defined purpose such as monitoring, prediction or decision support. The required update frequency follows that purpose: a temperature-monitoring task and a long-term maintenance study need diff

documents.title: Mathematical reminders for reduced models :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Mathematical reminders for reduced models This short reminder adapts the notation and ingredients slides (PDF). It supplies the prerequisites used in the proofs, not an additional theory course. Keep the symbol and norm guide beside it. Continue to Riesz representation when you need to compute a residual norm. Inner products and induced norms A real vector space is closed under sums and scalar multiplication. An inner product \((w,v)_X\) is bilinear, symmetric, and positive definite: \((v,v)_X>0\) for nonzero \(v\). It defines \[\|v\|_X=\sqrt{(v,v)_X},\qquad |(w,v)_X|\leq\|w\|_X\|v\|_X.\] The second formula is Cauchy–Schwarz. A Hilbert space is an inner-product space complete in this norm: limits of Cauchy sequences remain in the space. Every finite-dimensional inner-product space is complete. If \((w,v)_X=0\), the vectors are orthogonal. Expanding the square gives Pythagoras: \[\|w+v\|_X^2=\|w\|_X^2+\|v\|_X^2.\] This identity explains why a POD reconstr

documents.title: Hilbert spaces, dual norms and Riesz representation :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Hilbert spaces, dual norms and Riesz representation A residual or a sensor is a rule acting on a state. A state norm measures vectors; a dual norm measures these rules. This page explains the connection needed to compute residual bounds and to construct data-assimilation updates. The notation guide distinguishes the fixed norm \(\|\cdot\|_X\) used here from the current-parameter energy norm (triple bars); the mathematical reminders introduce the weak PDE. Course route: read through the matrix example before session 3. The function-space example and the existence proof are supplementary reading. The efficient offline/online implementation of a certificate is separate advanced reading. From inner products to linear functionals A real inner-product space has a symmetric bilinear product \((u,v)_X\) that is positive on every nonzero vector. It defines the norm \(\|v\|_X=\sqrt{(v,v)_X}\). A Hilbert space is complete in this norm: every Cauchy sequence converg

documents.title: DEIM: POD-based empirical interpolation :: Reduced Models & Digital Twins
documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf DEIM: POD-based empirical interpolation Read non-affinity and EIM first. DEIM constructs a POD basis of source or nonlinear-term snapshots, then chooses interpolation coordinates for that basis. The state basis and nonlinear-term basis have different roles and generally different dimensions. The source grid has \(N_q\) evaluation points. The term is \(g\), its retained POD basis \(U_m\), and the selected-row matrix \(T=P_m^TU_m\). Here \(P_m\) contains coordinate vectors selecting the magic points, and \(D_m\) is the DEIM interpolation operator defined below. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Non-affinity and empirical interpolation An affine decomposition separates parameter dependence from spatial operators: \[A(\mu)=\sum_{q=1}^{Q_a}\Theta_q^a(\mu)A_q, \qquad f(\mu)=\sum_{q=1}^{Q_f}\Theta_q^f(\mu)f_q.\] The worked affine prediction example shows exactly which arrays are stored and used at a query. For small fixed numbers of terms, projected matrices and vectors are assembled offline. A moving Gaussian source or a nonlinear constitutive law generally lacks such a small exact decomposition. Evaluating the entire source or nonlinear residual online can then dominate the reduced solve. Empirical interpolation constructs a separable approximation whose coefficients are determined from selected evaluations. documents.content: Edit this Page Download as .pdf Greedy reduced bases and POD Read POD and residual certificates first. POD minimizes an average squared projection error for a declared snapshot distribution and state metric. A reduced-basis greedy algorithm instead seeks a space that controls the largest estimated reduced-solve error on a finite training set. Neither criterion alone guarantees accuracy outside that set.
